name: Phulay Bay, A Ritz Carlton Reserve
positioning: Phulay Bay, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve: villas and pavilions with personal pools and butler service, on the Andaman Sea coast near Krabi
best_for: Couples who want private dining and a butler-led stay
Travelers who want guided nature and cultural outings around Krabi

facts.text: Each guest has a personal butler, called a Ton Hong, who can arrange bespoke experiences.
The villas and pavilions blur the line between indoors and outdoors and have personal pools and ocean and garden views.
The accommodations include traditional Thai design elements such as hand-painted panels.
The villas have rainforest showers and outdoor bath facilities.
A private fine dining restaurant serves traditional Southern Thai cooking family-style, with several items presented at once.
Complimentary breakfast is available to hotel guests.
The spa has eleven treatment rooms, including outdoor terraces, with views of the lagoon.
The spa has a vitality pool.
Guests can take long-tail boat rides to Hong Island.
A cultural journey includes a long-tail boat through mangroves to the fishing village of Koh Klang, where guests can try batik painting.

highlights.text: Phulay Bay describes itself as the world's first Ritz-Carlton Reserve.
Sala Srichan offers a private dining experience lit by 2,000 candles, with a multi-course menu by the Executive Chef paired with Champagne.
A guided two-hour hike to Dragon Crest Mountain takes guests through rainforest to a summit viewpoint.
The hotel collaborates with the Krabi Elephant House Sanctuary on a guided nature experience.

considerations.text: Condé Nast Traveler says the grounds are sprawling and perhaps more easily explored on wheels, and staff will chauffeur guests in golf carts.
Condé Nast Traveler says the beach is disappointing, with rocky shallows and a bay marred by a dredging complex.
The closest airport is Krabi International Airport, approximately 40 km from the hotel.
